brief: For Slovenian banking-technology vendors the public record is almost entirely vendor-authored: with systemic banks private and outside procurement law, the only disclosures of who supplies what come from vendors' own reference pages, case studies and press releases. The single richest find is HRC d.o.o. (Hibis core banking), whose 'O nas' page names eleven Slovenian financial institutions and whose 'Aktualno' section documents core-system migrations at Deželna banka Slovenije, OTP banka and Nova KBM — exactly the procurement-invisible events this cell exists to capture; Halcom (Hal E-Bank, e-signature), Mikrografija (mDocs/mSign at Delavska hranilnica), Comtrade SI, Bankart (bank-owned card processor) and Payten/Asseco SEE plus Euronet on the ATM/POS side complete the core actor map. Because most of these vendors are private and publish little themselves, three indirect channels carry disproportionate weight: the Računalniške novice press-release wire (often the only archived copy of a vendor's bank announcement), Monitor.si trade journalism, and financial/registry aggregators (Bizi, CompanyWall, AJPES) where revenue jumps proxy for large project wins; bank app-store publisher fields are a cheap, reliable vendor fingerprint. Local-language search proved mandatory and decisive — the identical English query returned only global SEO listicles, while the Slovenian one surfaced HRC and a named bank migration on the first page.
